Criteri ecografici di sospetto di un lin:
Ultrasound criteria of suspicion for a lymph node: round shape (short/long axis ratio > 0.5), absence of the hyperechoic fatty hilum, peripheral or chaotic vascularity on Doppler, necrosis (anechoic areas), microcalcifications (typical of metastases from papillary thyroid carcinoma), blurred margins if there is extracapsular extension. Size alone is a weak criterion.

In lung carcinoma a metastatic supraclavicular or scalene lymph node is N3 (stage at least IIIB-IIIC, IVA-B if there are distant metastases); a higher cervical lymph node, outside the supraclavicular and scalene region, instead counts as a distant metastasis (M1). Here the level is not indicated. Ultrasound-guided biopsy is a minimally invasive way to obtain histology and stage together. Before inserting the needle, the vessels (jugular vein, carotid) are identified and a safe path is chosen; in the images with the needle the tip is seen inside the lymph node.
